title: Schorach ani wenowach, benoith Hierushaloim.
html_source:
“I am black yet comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem” from the Song of Songs. Zoe, described as having odalisk lips, is singing the words from the bride’s apology and song to her lover. In the biblical passage Israel is the bride confessing her own unworthiness, her sins and the anger of her brothers and sisters.

Musical Allusions in the Works of James Joyce: Early Poetry through Ulysses
By Zack R. Bowen
